name: Coronation of Pepin the Short
summary: Pepin III ('the Short'), son of Charles Martel and mayor of the palace to the last Merovingian king Childeric III, asks Pope Zachary a pointed question: who should be king, the one who holds power or the one who merely carries the title? The Pope answers in Pepin's favor. Childeric III is deposed and sent to a monastery; Pepin is anointed king of the Franks by St. Boniface, and subsequently by Pope Stephen II in 754. This is the first papal coronation of a Frankish king and establishes the precedent that papal sanction legitimizes royal power.

_quarry.structural_significance: Ends the Merovingian dynasty and founds the Carolingian dynasty that produces Charlemagne; the papal-Frankish alliance becomes the cornerstone of medieval Western politics; Pepin's Donation (754) creates the Papal States as a temporal kingdom, giving the papacy independent political power; the precedent that popes can sanction rulers, and by implication depose them, fuels the Investiture Controversy three centuries later
